newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Atlas Copco dips on news of weak Europe.
newsitem.headline: Atlas Copco dips on news of weak Europe.

text.p: Swedish engineering firm Atlas Copco shares slipped in early trade on Wednesday after the company released some details of its first quarter performance at its annual general meeting on Tuesday after the market closed.
At 0900 GMT Atlas Copco shares were three crowns lower at 196 crowns.
Outgoing chief executive Michael Treschow told the AGM that the company's sales rose six percent to 6.41 billion crowns while order intake rose eight percent to 7.22 billion crowns.
However he said the construction market in Europe continued to show no signs of improvement.

"Our estimate is that demand for the European construction market will remain weak. The manufacturing industry in Europe could, however, develop somewhat better during the year," Treschow told the AGM.
Analysts said this was the cause of the dip in the share price.
"I think people are a bit disappointed that there is no sign of a pick up in the construction market in Europe," analyst Peter Lawrence from Dresdner Kleinwort Benson told Reuters.
"The order intake figure is not bad in itself."
Atlas Copco will release its first quarter report on April 28.
